sections.heading: Client Updates
sections.summary: Teams reported work on EIP-8411, Waggle integration, new networking stacks (Silver, Lambda beacon client, Lodestar Zig stack), and PQ protocol research.
sections.body:
- jxs: Continuing Waggle research, working on EIP-8411 implementation, exploring the interface boundary between application and network layers.
- Lighthouse (Kamil): Has an EIP-8411 implementation in Lighthouse using Waggle; ran simulations showing promising bandwidth savings.
- Prysm (Aarsh Shah): Beginning to prototype EIP-8411 and diving into Waggle; will start by reviewing Daniel's PR integrating Waggle for 1-to-1 communication.
- Nethermind (FLCL): Improved P2P in .NET; exploring protocols for more usable light clients; interested in PQ-related protocols and implementations; will review EIP-8411 in detail.
- Geth (Felix): Mempool improvements ongoing; working on QUIC transport for EL, shared networking specification repository, and a plan for post-quantum ENRs and Discovery v5 transition (to be posted to Discord soon).
- Lodestar (cayman): Building a new networking stack in Zig tailored to Ethereum workloads rather than generic libp2p; JS libp2p side moving to maintenance mode.
- Silver/Gattaca (vlad): Announced Silver, a new client with a libp2p-compatible but non-libp2p networking stack; working on a production-ready Rust [seacast library](https://github.com/gattaca-com/seacast-rs), noting specs are still in flight.
- Lambda (Pablo): Launched a Beacon Chain client, presented in Cambridge; running experiments measuring PQ signature sizes and their impact on networking.

sections.heading: Meeting Time Change
sections.summary: The call will move approximately 5 hours earlier to accommodate Europe/Asia/Australia participants, though Lodestar Americas-based members cannot attend at the new time.
sections.body:
- Kamil proposed moving the bi-weekly call ~5 hours earlier to improve coverage for Europe, Southeast Asia, and Australia time zones.
- Lodestar's cayman and Matthew Keil (both in Americas time zones) confirmed they cannot make a call 5 hours earlier; Matthew noted he will be back in Asia starting January.
- Kamil acknowledged the trade-off but noted most regular attendees can still join; rotating times was considered but rejected to avoid confusion.
- Decision: the invite will be updated in the protocol calendar to the earlier time; additional breakout calls at different times may be scheduled for important discussions.

sections.heading: Unified Networking Specification Repository
sections.summary: Felix presented a merged EL/CL networking spec repo with version-based (not fork-based) organization, draft/current/legacy statuses, and plans to house Waggle, seacast, and QUIC transport specs.
sections.body:
- Felix demoed a new repository that merges the devp2p (EL) and consensus-specs (CL) networking specifications into a single location, organized by layer: Transport, Discovery, Execution, and Consensus (with a planned Broadcast category for Waggle/seacast).
- CL networking specs are currently versioned by fork in consensus-specs, making it hard to find a fully up-to-date complete spec; the new repo maintains a single "current" document with a changelog, plus frozen "legacy" versions for older protocol iterations.
- EL specs already use protocol version numbers (e.g., eth/72); Felix wants to bring this model to CL networking as well, allowing protocol updates independent of hard forks.
- Draft/experimental specs can be merged early into the repo under naming conventions like `eth-eip-XXXX` or `draft-title`, avoiding long-lived open PRs and enabling collaborative iteration on main branch.
  - An example experimental spec for Heze (future fork, not yet scoped) was included as version 7 of the CL networking protocol.
- Csaba highlighted the importance of EIP-based naming to avoid confusion from self-assigned protocol version numbers, noting there are already 3 competing eth/73 EIPs.
- cayman cautioned that moving CL specs from fork-based to versioned organization is a big change requiring buy-in from active CL spec contributors to avoid backlash.
- Matthew Keil (Lodestar) raised concern that CL networking changes are fork-gated in client code; introducing a separate version dimension would add implementation complexity.
  - Felix clarified the goal is not to remove fork-based versioning but to maintain a complete, always-current spec document and allow non-fork networking changes (e.g., new broadcast protocols) to be tracked.
- Felix confirmed validation functions for gossip will remain in consensus-specs (fork-versioned); only message definitions and stack descriptions move to the new repo.
- Planned contents: Waggle spec, seacast spec, QUIC transport spec, and a libp2p adapter spec that clarifies how libp2p is currently configured for CL use.
- Repository location TBD (Ethereum GitHub org or ethp2p GitHub org); Felix will share the repo in Discord for broader feedback before considering an ACD presentation.

sections.heading: QUIC-Only Transport Vision and libp2p Dependency
sections.summary: Felix outlined a long-term plan to migrate EL and CL to a shared QUIC-only transport with no libp2p dependency; jxs pushed back on deprecating TCP.
sections.body:
- Felix stated the long-term goal is a shared QUIC-only transport for EL and CL, eliminating libp2p entirely; multistream-select over QUIC is minimal enough to re-specify directly.
- jxs pushed back: their client drove QUIC adoption and mplex deprecation, but has no plans to deprecate TCP with yamux — it works, and QUIC still has middlebox issues.
- Felix acknowledged the disagreement but argued QUIC provides the best package for post-quantum security and a minimal, fully-controllable stack.
- Waggle's spec does not deeply depend on libp2p (confirmed by Felix referencing discussions with Sukun); jxs agreed the spec is transport-agnostic but noted current working implementations rely on libp2p's multistream-select and existing network primitives.
- jxs emphasized that rewriting working infrastructure should only be justified by concrete requirements (e.g., PQ), not pursued for its own sake.
- cayman noted Lodestar's new networking stack is also QUIC-only, and that "libp2p-compatible" need not mean using a generic libp2p library.
- Felix proposed continuing this stack-direction discussion over future P2P calls rather than resolving it now.

sections.heading: WebTX: Browser-to-EL Transaction Submission
sections.summary: Geth's Bosul demoed WebTX, a QUIC/WebTransport-based sub-protocol letting browsers submit transactions directly to EL nodes without RPC endpoints; it is already merged in Geth.
sections.body:
- WebTX allows browsers to connect to EL nodes via WebTransport over QUIC and submit transactions without an RPC endpoint.
- ENRs carry a new `QH` field containing a certificate hash for certificate pinning; two certificates are announced (current 2-week period + next 2-week period) for seamless rotation.
- Connection flow: browser opens a WebTransport session, sends an identity proof challenge (random 32-byte nonce); server signs it to prove it holds the node key; browser verifies before submitting.
- The protocol has only two messages: TransactionSubmit and TransactionResult.
- Anti-DoS measures: browser connections limited to 10-second lifetime; connection is severed after first message; invalid transactions trigger IP-based rejection for a cooldown period.
- Spec PR: [devp2p #276](https://github.com/ethereum/devp2p/pull/276) — currently covers only the QUIC transport layer, not the WebTX sub-protocol messages.
- WebTX is merged in Geth and can be enabled on mainnet today for browser-based transaction submission.
- Future plans: add peer exchange so browsers can discover more nodes beyond bootstrap ENRs; experiment with PQTLS (browsers may already support it via QUIC); long-term consideration of onion routing for transaction propagation.
- Felix explained the write-only focus: server-side resource requirements for reads are too high and incentives unclear; for reads, wallets can use multiple RPC providers with proofs. For writes, users currently have no way to know their transaction reaches the mempool.
- FLCL asked whether this helps with wallet read requests (logs, state, simulation); confirmed it does not — write-only by design.
- Felix noted browser-side discovery doesn't need the full discv5 stack since the worst case for a failed peer exchange is simply re-submitting the transaction elsewhere.

sections.heading: XMSS Signature Broadcast Simulations
sections.summary: Kamil presented simulation results showing that reducing gossipsub mesh degree and introducing hash-based turn-taking between peers can significantly cut duplicate messages during PQ attestation propagation.
sections.body:
- Motivation: PQ (XMSS) signatures are much larger than BLS; reducing duplicate message transmissions becomes critical for bandwidth.
- Simulation setup: ~3,700 hosts, 32K validators (worst-case per-slot with 1M total validators), geographic distribution modeled; regular nodes assumed 50 Mbps up / 100 Mbps down (more optimistic than EIP-7870).
- Reducing mesh degree from 8 to 4 dropped average duplicates per first copy from ~4 to ~2.5 with no reliability loss; mesh degree 3 caused some peers to stop receiving messages.
- EIP-8334 bundled broadcast (collecting attestations every 20ms) was applied but provides less savings with large PQ signatures since the attestation data deduplication benefit shrinks.
- Turn-taking optimization: for each mesh link, both peers hash the attestation message + both peer IDs to deterministically assign one peer as "pusher" and the other as "waiter," preventing the same message from traveling in both directions.
  - With a 1-second wait period, duplicates dropped further to ~1.6.
  - Adding an announce-then-request pattern with 200ms request delay achieved the best results: low duplicates and faster propagation than baseline gossipsub.
- Kamil noted these optimizations are much easier to implement in Waggle (where peers are individually addressable) than in gossipsub (where messages are forwarded to the entire mesh).
- FLCL observed that peer-ID-hash ordering is also useful for resolving simultaneous reconnection races.
- Mikel (ProbeLab) cautioned that simulations only test the happy path; resilience under adversarial conditions (non-forwarding peers, eclipse attacks, delayed messages) also needs evaluation.
  - Kamil agreed churn and adversarial scenarios should be simulated for gossipsub, the turn-taking approach, and Waggle.
- cayman urged running simulations with EIP-7870 bandwidth assumptions, arguing that bad results under those constraints would provide objective justification to update the EIP.
  - Kamil argued EIP-7870's numbers (from 21 months ago) are likely outdated per Nielsen's Law and survey data showing validators have higher bandwidth; favors updating EIP-7870 but acknowledged the debate is ongoing.

sections.heading: EIP-8411 and Waggle Adoption Status
sections.summary: EIP-8411 is CFI'd; a Waggle-based PR and a Lighthouse implementation exist for review, but adoption scope may change as Hegota fork is reconsidered.
sections.body:
- Daniel's PR to update EIP-8411 to use Waggle: [EIPs PR #12671](https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/12671).
- Lighthouse implementation of EIP-8411 with Waggle: [Lighthouse PR #10604](https://github.com/sigp/lighthouse/pull/10604).
- Kamil encouraged CL developers to review the Lighthouse PR to gauge Waggle implementation complexity, as future discussions will address whether to adopt Waggle.
- EIP-8411 is currently CFI for the Hegota fork, but the fork's scope may be reconsidered; the practical meaning of CFI status is unclear pending upcoming ACDC calls.
- Csaba noted he is preparing a PR to clarify EIP-8411's chunking descriptor and a Reed-Solomon scheme (had to leave the call before the topic was discussed in depth).
